candidates.statement: A BLA submitted under section 351(k) (a “351(k) BLA”) of the PHS Act must contain, among 101 other things, information demonstrating that the biological product is biosimilar to a reference 102 product based upon data derived from analytical studies, animal studies, and a clinical study or 103 studies (see section 351(k)(2)(A)(i)(I) of the PHS Act), unless FDA has determined that an 104 element described in section 351(k)(2)(A)(i)(I) is unnecessary (see section 351(k)(2)(A)(ii) of 105 the PHS Act). To meet the standard for “interchangeability,” an applicant must provide 106 sufficient information to demonstrate biosimilarity to the reference product and also to 107 demonstrate that the biological product can be expected to produce the same clinical result as the 108 reference product in any given patient, and if the biological product is administered more than 109 once to an individual, the risk in terms of safety or diminished efficacy of alternating or 110 switching between the use of the biological product and the reference product is not greater than 111 the risk of using the reference product without such alternation or switch (see section 351(k)(4) 112 of the PHS Act). Interchangeable products may be substituted for the reference product without 113 the intervention of the prescribing health care provider (see section 351(i)(3) of the PHS Act). 114
candidates.context: Section 351(i) of the PHS Act defines biosimilarity to mean “that the biological product is highly 95 similar to the reference product notwithstanding minor differences in clinically inactive 96 components” and that “there are no clinically meaningful differences between the biological 97 product and the reference product in terms of the safety, purity, and potency of the product” (see 98 section 351(i)(2) of the PHS Act). 99 “Question-and-Answer” Guidance Format 116

candidates.statement: 4 In addition to the requirement under section 351(k)(4) that FDA determine that the information submitted in the application or the supplement is sufficient to show that the biological product “is biosimilar to the reference product,” FDA must also find that the proposed product “can be expected to produce the same clinical result as the reference product in any given patient,” and that “for a biological product that is administered more than once to an individual, the risk in terms of safety or diminished efficacy of alternating or switching between use of the biological product and the reference product is not greater than the risk of using the reference product without such alternation or switch” in order to license the proposed product as an interchangeable biosimilar.
candidates.context: A.I.25 To support licensure of an interchangeable biosimilar under section 351(k) of the PHS 157 Act, an applicant must show that the product meets the standards described in section 158 351(k)(4). 4 Among the specified criteria that must be met to be licensed as an 159 interchangeable biosimilar under section 351(k)(4), the applicant must show that the 160 biological product is “biosimilar to the reference product.” Thus, there may be 161 situations in which the data and information provided in a BLA seeking licensure as 162 an interchangeable biosimilar can support licensure of the product as a biosimilar 163 product but not as an interchangeable biosimilar. 164

candidates.statement: As an initial matter, if a BLA submitted under section 351(k) of the PHS Act is 166 intended to support licensure as an interchangeable biosimilar, the BLA submission 167 should contain an affirmative statement to that effect. If a BLA submission does not 168 contain such a statement, the Agency plans to evaluate the BLA for licensure only as 169 a biosimilar product. In other words, the Agency intends to evaluate whether the 170 proposed product meets the requirements for licensure as an interchangeable 171 biosimilar only if the 351(k) BLA indicates at the time of submission that it contains 172 information intended to demonstrate that the product meets the standards described in 173 section 351(k)(4) for licensure as an interchangeable biosimilar. This approach 174 provides for a more efficient and predictable review of BLAs. 175
